meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: Everyday verb for eating a meal or food; honorific equivalent is 드시다.

examples.trans: Let's eat lunch together.
Did you eat breakfast?

meanings.note: Someone who started earlier than you.

examples.trans: school senior
My senior bought me a meal.
I want to eat (honorific) right now.
How about trying to eat (honorific) together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Auxiliary adjective attached to a verb stem with -고 (-고 싶다).

examples.trans: I want to go to Korea.
I want to drink a cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.
Did you hear about this opinion?
I was busy today because of opinion.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.
Did you hear about this black-bean noodles?
I was busy today because of black-bean noodles.

빼다.gloss: to take out; to remove; to exclude

meanings.en: to take out; to remove; to exclude
meanings.note: Used for removing someone from a schedule or taking something out.
Used in arithmetic.

examples.trans: Please take my name off the list.
I took the key out of my pocket.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
Did you hear about this yesterday?
I was busy today because of yesterday.
I want to stayed up all night right now.
How about trying to stayed up all night together tomorrow?
Did you hear about this stomach, insides?
I was busy today because of stomach, insides.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

좋다.gloss: to be good, to be nice

examples.trans: I feel really good today.
It's nice to take a walk in the morning.
Did you hear about this kimchi stew?
I was busy today because of kimchi stew.

meanings.note: noun eye

examples.trans: Eye hurts.
Eyes are big.
It really is white compared to what I thought.
Especially today, it is white and nice.

I was busy today because of T-shirt.

examples.trans: I wore a black coat today.
It's cold, so please dress warmly.

I was busy today because of hamburgers.

meanings.note: noun director

examples.trans: Director-nim.
Director's office.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!
Did you hear about this muscle?
I was busy today because of muscle.
I want to end up right now.
How about trying to end up together tomorrow?

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Used by a younger male to address an older brother or close older male friend/colleague.

examples.trans: Hey, do you have time tonight?
My older brother is an office worker.
Let's have a drink together today.
I worked hard to have a drink yesterday too.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.
Did you hear about this all sorts of?
I was busy today because of all sorts of.
Did you hear about this sights, spectacles?
I was busy today because of sights, spectacles.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.
